summary: Deployed a self-signed-CA-backed HTTPS service on node1 port 8443 that renews its TLS certificate automatically before expiry and hot-picks-up each renewed cert without dropping connections or restarting; completed the single-node restart/recovery evidence protocol.
actions_performed: Surveyed node1 (RHEL 7.9, no internet/yum repos, no nginx/httpd/python3; only python2.7.5 with ssl.SSLContext and openssl 1.0.2k available)
Built a local demo CA at /opt/https-rotate/ca (ca.key/ca.crt, index.txt/serial) to sign short-lived leaf certs
Wrote /opt/https-rotate/gen-cert.sh: issues a 300s-lifetime leaf cert, renewing only when fewer than 180s of validity remain (openssl x509 -checkend), atomically swapping tls.key/tls.crt into place

Wrote /opt/https-rotate/serve.py: python2 threaded HTTPS server that builds a fresh SSLContext from the current cert/key files on every newly accepted TCP connection, so a renewed cert is served on the very next request with no process restart
Installed and enabled systemd units https-rotate.service (the server) and https-rotate-renew.timer/.service (renewal check every 60s, Persistent=true)
Fixed a python2 SocketServer.accept() bug found on first boot, redeployed, verified curl -k https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns 200 'ok'
Observed two live automatic renewal cycles (cert serial 1000->1001->1002) via a polling loop while https-rotate.service's MainPID (2428) stayed constant, proving hot cert pickup without restart

Captured pre-reboot boot_id/health baseline, ran sudo systemctl reboot on node1, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a new boot_id, confirmed both systemd units auto-started, and observed a further renewal cycle post-reboot (serial 1002->1003) with HTTPS continuing to serve 200s

evidence.requirement: HTTPS served on port 8443 with a valid cert
evidence.summary: After fixing the accept() bug and restarting the service, curl -k to https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returns HTTP 200 'ok'; openssl s_client shows the served cert serial=1000, notAfter=14:31:04Z, matching the locally issued leaf cert.

evidence.requirement: Certificate renewed automatically before it expires
evidence.summary: Cert serial advanced 1000->1001 before the original 14:31:04Z expiry (last-renewed 14:28:40Z, new expiry 14:33:40Z, confirmed via live TLS handshake), and a second cycle 1001->1002 and later 1002->1003 was captured, all triggered automatically by https-rotate-renew.timer with no manual intervention.

evidence.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests (no restart)
evidence.summary: Poll log shows serial 1001->1002 transition with http=200 on every 20s check, and systemctl show -p MainPID reported the unchanged PID 2428 across both renewal cycles, proving the running process served the newly rotated cert without restarting.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id d72bd4ec-4e55-42df-9c71-99b4f4ace0ec, both systemd units active, cert serial=1002 valid, and HTTPS returning 200 immediately before the reboot.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: restart acknowledged and boot identity changed
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged before the connection dropped; subsequent exec calls timed out during the reboot window and then succeeded again reporting a new boot_id 41f1cd47-f42d-46ed-8ba7-ca8f93bcee75, proving an actual restart occurred.

evidence.requirement: node1 mandatory restart evidence: post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, https-rotate.service and https-rotate-renew.timer were active again (auto-started, new MainPID 871), the existing cert/data on disk was intact (serial=1002 still valid), HTTPS answered 200, and a further automatic renewal (serial 1002->1003) was observed post-reboot, confirming full end-to-end recovery of the rotation pipeline.
